title: Asymptotic size of a largest Sidon subset of an integer interval
difficulty_reason: The upper bound uses short-index differences, lower bounds their sum by distinctness, and telescopes it from above before choosing the cutoff. The lower bound uses the full CRT family in Section 3.2 and the original quadratic-factorization argument, then passes from odd primes to all large intervals. The two bounds establish the same asymptotic constant without a conditional prime-gap hypothesis.

selected_claim: The full original Theorem 5, that the maximum size of a Sidon subset of [n] is asymptotic to sqrt(n).
source_caveats: The opening of the lower proof on p11 prints 1 <= t < p-1 alongside p-1 elements. The same fixed PDF pp4–5 directly defines and counts the family for 1 <= t < p. P11 itself identifies the family at the end as Ruzsa(p,theta,1).

The p11 congruences, primitive-root argument and quadratic uniqueness are the author’s original text. The theorem and full printed proof are retained. Pp4–5 are explicit selected author support for the p-1 element family and its Sidon property. There is no separate erratum among the selected materials.

The lower construction is due to Ruzsa, cited as [59] on p26. O’Bryant supplies the upper and lower proof on pp10–11 and gives the full lower family on pp4–5. The underlying historical attributions are retained in the PDF.
